raw_response:
I'm 65 this year, and I've been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets the county sends around and I understand what they mean by "jointing stage" and "boll filling," but honestly, most of what I know comes from doing it myself and watching my neighbors. My wife is still healthy and works the fields with me. My son and his wife work in a factory in Handan and send some money home for the grandchildren, but I don't like relying on that — this farm is my responsibility, and it needs to pay for itself.

I split my 5 mu into **3 mu of cotton** and **2 mu of wheat-maize double crop**. Cotton is my cash crop — the money from selling seed cotton pays for medicine, repairs, and whatever the grandchildren need. The wheat and maize are for our own flour and for feeding the chickens. I never put all my land into one crop; that's too risky. If the bollworms hit the cotton hard, at least I still have grain in the barn.

Right now it's late April, so I'm busy with cotton planting. The wheat went in last October and is greening up. I'll harvest it in early June and immediately plant maize — the window between wheat coming off and maize going in is usually less than a week, so I have everything ready.

### Cotton (3 mu)

I buy improved cotton seed from the county supply store, about 1.5 jin per mu. The extension agent keeps pushing hybrid seed, but it's 50 yuan per mu and I don't see the yield jump on my small plot to justify that. I plough the field deep in spring with my small tractor — cotton roots need loose soil. Before planting I spread about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and work it in. The county booklet says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've learned over the years that if I push it to about 14 kg total N, the bolls fill better and the plants don't yellow in August. So I topdress with another 10 kg of urea per mu at early flowering, plus a little extra potassium — cotton is hungry for K. 

I irrigate twice from my well: once at flowering and once at boll filling. Each time the electricity meter spins fast — costs about 35 yuan per mu — so three times is too expensive for me. But skipping that second irrigation is gambling; I tried it in 2019 and lost almost a third of my yield. Bollworms are my biggest worry, so I spray insecticide four times and herbicide once. Cotton picking is labor-intensive. My wife and I do most of it, but in September and October when the bolls are bursting open, I hire a neighbor for 2 days to help. That's 150 yuan per day, but at my age I can't pick 3 mu by myself without breaking my back. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather is normal.

### Winter Wheat (2 mu)

I planted an improved wheat variety last October, about 15 kg per mu. Before sowing I spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu and tilled it in. Now it's spring, and the wheat is at jointing. I topdress with about 10 kg of urea per mu — I watch the color, and if it looks a bit yellow at the base I put it down. Two years ago I skipped the topdress because fertilizer prices jumped, and I lost maybe 50 kg per mu. That was a hard lesson. Fertilizer is expensive, but a thin wheat crop is a disaster I can't afford. 

I irrigate twice: jointing water and heading water. The well water is costly, but wheat is our main food — I can't let it dry out at heading. I spray herbicide once in spring. My wife and I handle all the labor. For harvest in early June, I hire the village combine — 60 yuan per mu — which is worth it because threshing by hand would take forever. I expect about 400 kg per mu.

### Summer Maize (2 mu)

The day after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 or something similar from the county store, about 2.5 kg per mu. There's no time for fancy tillage. If the ground is soft I plant directly into the wheat stubble; if it's hard, one quick pass with the rotary tiller, then plant immediately with the hand planter. All the fertilizer goes in at planting: about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the seed furrow. The season is too short for split application, and with only 2 mu I'm not making extra trips.

I irrigate once at the big flare stage if the summer rains haven't come. Sometimes I irrigate a second time at silking, but only if it's very dry — electricity bills add up. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once. My wife and I do everything ourselves. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

### The tradeoffs

Total input costs this year come to about **1,600 yuan**. Seed is roughly 270 yuan, fertilizer about 650 yuan, pesticide about 250 yuan, irrigation electricity about 300 yuan, and the combine harvest another 120 yuan. That's a lot of money for a 5-mu farm. My son sends home about 1,000 yuan a month, which covers living expenses, but I don't touch that for the farm — this land has to support itself. At 65, I'm not as strong as I was twenty years ago, and my knees hurt after a day of bending over in the cotton field. But I know every corner of these 5 mu. I don't take big risks anymore. I do what worked last year, and the year before, and the year before that.
